name: Land steeper than 15% (%)
plain: Out of every 100 parts of the area's land, how many are steeper than 15%: where building and farming begin to need terraces or special design.
definition: The share of the area's 10 m cells whose slope is more than 15%, by Horn's method on the USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second elevation model.
geography: 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico; also 901 barrios

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt by hand (python slope.py) when USGS replaces an elevation tile, which happens only when new lidar arrives.

method: slope.py reads the USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second elevation tiles over Puerto Rico in windows of 0.1 degree (raster.py) and computes the slope of every 10 m cell by Horn's method, with the cell's size in metres at its latitude, as rise over run x 100; a cell next to one with no height has no slope. The cells are counted in blocks of 6 x 6 (about 60 m); a block belongs to the barrio that holds its centre (the nearest within 100 m off the coast), and blocks in no barrio (the sea) are left out. Municipios and Puerto Rico pool their barrios' cells. Checks at every build: Puerto Rico's share steeper than 30% between 15% and 55%; Jayuya, Orocovis and Barranquitas steeper than Puerto Rico; Cataño with less than 5% of its land steeper than 15%; the cells counted cover 97% to 110% of the barrios' Census land area.
source_detail: USGS 3D Elevation Program, 1/3 arc-second (about 10 m) seamless DEM, tiles USGS_13_n18w066_20260722.tif, USGS_13_n18w067_20260722.tif, USGS_13_n18w068_20260722.tif, USGS_13_n19w066_20260722.tif, USGS_13_n19w067_20260722.tif, USGS_13_n19w068_20260722.tif; barrio outlines of the observatory's crosswalk (Census 2020).
how_to_read: Puerto Rico: 61.7%. Highest: Maricao (95.4%), Orocovis (93.7%), Adjuntas (92.7%). Lowest: Loíza (1.2%), Cataño (2.0%).
caveats: Heights are of the bare ground at about 10 m: cuts, retaining walls and terraces narrower than a cell are smoothed out, and a road on a bridge reads the ground below.
A block of about 60 m across a barrio's edge counts whole in the barrio that holds its centre.
Inland water (lagoons, reservoirs) inside a barrio's outline counts as flat land.
The thresholds are planning guides, not rules for a site: whether a parcel can be built on depends on its soil, geology and drainage, and on the regulations.

name: Slope (USGS 3DEP, image of about 60 m blocks)
plain: A map of how steep the ground is, darker for steeper, from the USGS 10 m elevation model. A slider shows only the land at or above a slope.
definition: slope_surface.png is an indexed Web Mercator image of 3730 x 1241 pixels of about 59 m: each pixel is the mean slope of the 10 m cells of one block of slope.py, on a fixed scale of 64 steps from 0% to 60% (steeper is drawn as 60%), transparent over the sea. slope_surface.json gives its corners, size and scale. The 2D map lays it at 75% opacity under the landslide and soil layers; the legend's slider leaves out the steps below a chosen slope, and a click on the map gives the slope of the block under the point.
geography: Puerto Rico, Vieques and Culebra (Mona, Monito and Desecheo are not drawn)
method: slope.py reads the USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second elevation tiles over Puerto Rico in windows of 0.1 degree (raster.py) and computes the slope of every 10 m cell by Horn's method, with the cell's size in metres at its latitude, as rise over run x 100; a cell next to one with no height has no slope. The cells are counted in blocks of 6 x 6 (about 60 m); a block belongs to the barrio that holds its centre (the nearest within 100 m off the coast), and blocks in no barrio (the sea) are left out. Municipios and Puerto Rico pool their barrios' cells. Checks at every build: Puerto Rico's share steeper than 30% between 15% and 55%; Jayuya, Orocovis and Barranquitas steeper than Puerto Rico; Cataño with less than 5% of its land steeper than 15%; the cells counted cover 97% to 110% of the barrios' Census land area.
source_detail: USGS 3D Elevation Program, 1/3 arc-second (about 10 m) seamless DEM, tiles USGS_13_n18w066_20260722.tif, USGS_13_n18w067_20260722.tif, USGS_13_n18w068_20260722.tif, USGS_13_n19w066_20260722.tif, USGS_13_n19w067_20260722.tif, USGS_13_n19w068_20260722.tif; barrio outlines of the observatory's crosswalk (Census 2020).
how_to_read: Pale is flat, dark brown is steep. Move the slider to 15% or 30% to see only the land steeper than that. The shares by barrio are in Explore.
caveats: Heights are of the bare ground at about 10 m: cuts, retaining walls and terraces narrower than a cell are smoothed out, and a road on a bridge reads the ground below.
Each pixel is the mean of a block of about 60 m, so a narrow steep bank inside a flatter block looks gentler than it is.

name: Contour lines (drawn from the terrain tiles)
plain: Lines that join points of the same height, drawn in the browser from the terrain tiles of the 3D view; closer lines as you zoom in.
definition: While the layer is on, the browser asks the AWS Terrain Tiles (Terrarium encoding, the source of the 3D view's terrain; in Puerto Rico from USGS 3DEP) for the tiles in view up to zoom 15, decodes each pixel's height ((R x 256 + G + B / 256) - 32768 m) and traces the contour lines with marching squares. The interval is 100 m up to zoom 11, 50 m at 12, 20 m at 13 and 10 m from 14; every fifth line is thicker. Nothing is stored in the observatory's files.
geography: Puerto Rico, Vieques, Culebra and Mona

coverage.frequency: Drawn each time the layer is shown; the terrain tiles change rarely.

method: js/terrain.js: marching squares on each 256 x 256 tile, the saddle cells split by the mean of their four corners; levels above 0 m only.
source_detail: AWS Open Data Terrain Tiles (Mapzen, Terrarium encoding): https://registry.opendata.aws/terrain-tiles/; in Puerto Rico from USGS 3DEP.
how_to_read: Lines close together mean steep ground; far apart, gentle ground. Read the thicker lines for the height in round numbers.
caveats: Lines are traced tile by tile, so a line can have a one-pixel gap where two tiles meet.
The terrain tiles are about 5 m at the closest zoom and are smoothed at the island's scale.
